newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKFE to set base for China-related futures soon.
newsitem.headline: HKFE to set base for China-related futures soon.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) will soon decide on a mixture of stocks on which to base its planned China-related stock index futures and options, chief executive Ivers Riley told Reuters in an interview.
"There are different varieties of China concepts, there are H-shares and there are the co-called red chips, so the idea is do you blend those or don't you blend those," Riley said.
"We are going to be very careful how we do that because there are pluses and minuses to how many (stocks) you include," he said, adding that those decisions would be taken shortly.
Riley said the futures and options contracts would be launched together, probably in the second half of 1997, following the success of Hang Seng Index options launched in 1993.
"The key is that the market is relatively small at the present time so we want to be very careful about not bringing that so soon that it can have a deleterious effect on the market," he added.

The HKFE has an agreement with HSI Services Ltd allowing the exchange to use the H-share index as a base for futures and options. Riley said if the exchange wanted to broaden the concept, it would cooperate with HSI.
"But there is no final decision that's going to happen at the moment," he added.
Riley said many investors are putting a large portion of their investments into China-related stocks. "Because the real attraction in Asia now is the growth in China," he said.
"The idea is, the best way to introduce products is when people care and people are caring now," Riley added.
